title: Testing a blind 3-AI jury vs human eyes on 150 HY-Motion 1.0 game animations
author: Evening-Crab4100
selftext:
We graded 150 single-take clips from Tencent's HY-Motion 1.0 on our Unreal Engine 5.9 mannequin using a simple pass, partial, and fail rubric. Every clip was evaluated by hand across eight gameplay categories with zero cherry-picking.

Before sharing our scores anywhere, we had three frontier AI models blindly grade the exact same 150 clips on the exact same rubric. Because Gemini 4 Neon is the only one of the three with native video capability to actually watch full 60fps motion, while Claude Fable 5.2 and GPT-6.2 Astra cannot ingest video natively and are limited to 8-frame image strips, we weighted Neon higher at 40% and gave Fable and Astra 30% each.

The gap between the AI jury and human eyes was wild, especially when Neon watched full 60fps video on a standing backflip hop that never inverted and still passed it cleanly, while the jury waved through stiff walks and broken skips. Curious how other devs here handle automated motion QA without watching every take by hand.
